_comment: THE TOKEN ROLE CONTRACT for /prove page themes. It is EMPIRICAL, not editorial: every role in
here is here because one or more of three INDEPENDENTLY-authored themes (NERV, AKIRA, WIRE) built
a token for it. Nothing was added because it seemed like a good idea. Where a theme's author
stated in their own :root comment which contract gap they were filling, that sentence is quoted
verbatim in `citation` — that is the authority for the role existing.
HOW A ROLE IS GRADED (mechanical — theme-roles.mjs recomputes it, this file never states a tier):
roleEvidence = how many of the 3 graded themes declared a token for the role, ANY spelling.
3 -> required   2 -> emerging   0..1 -> proposed
nameEvidence = how many of them spelled it `canonical`. The gap between roleEvidence and
nameEvidence IS the convergence debt — it is the answer to 'what do we do with the prefixes'.
HOW `canonical` IS PICKED (mechanical, so nobody's taste decides a name):
1. kit-incumbent   — the kit (proof-theme.css) already has the role; its spelling wins, because
the cheapest convergence is the one that renames the fewest live files.
2. theme-consensus — the kit has no such role, but >=2 graded themes chose the SAME spelling
(after stripping their namespace prefix).
3. sole-author     — the kit has no such role and exactly ONE graded theme built it, so that
theme's spelling stands unopposed. Weak authority: it is one proposal.
4. undecided       — >=2 themes built the role and no two agreed on a name. `canonical` is null
ON PURPOSE. Naming it would be an editorial act, and for the roles that
land here (absence, chrome ground, provenance, radius, texture) the name
carries a design ruling. These are listed for a HUMAN to rule on; the gate
reports them loudly and never fails on them.
WHAT `spellings` IS: the observed token name in each theme, PREFIX ALREADY STRIPPED (NERV's
--nv-focus is recorded as --focus; the prefix map lives in theme-roles.sources.json). null means
that theme built no token for the role. theme-roles.mjs RE-DERIVES this from the files and errors
if it disagrees — this file is a recorded observation, not an unchecked promise.
WHAT THIS CONTRACT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO: it never compares VALUES. NERV's spacing ladder is
derived from a 22px mono line box and the kit's from a 27.5px rhythm, so the SAME role carries
DIFFERENT values and any value-matcher mis-pairs them silently. Roles are matched by the author's
declared role comment and by name, and by nothing else.
ROLES CONSIDERED AND DELIBERATELY OMITTED (could not be mapped without guessing, see the build
report): depth/shadow recipes (NERV --lift/--sink vs AKIRA --depth-once vs WIRE --plane/--recess
vs kit --shadow-card are four different SHAPES of value, not four spellings of one role); the
recessed/second ground (NERV --well is 'imported material only', AKIRA --stock-2 is 'a pressed
region', kit --card-2 is just a second card — three different meanings).

mandates.statement: Wherever colour carries meaning, a non-colour channel must carry it too.
mandates.note: No single role is 3-of-3 here, and that is the finding: all three themes met the mandate, each with a DIFFERENT mechanism (NERV varies hatch pitch, AKIRA varies areal ink coverage, WIRE swaps mark shape). The mandate is therefore a disjunction over roles, not a role. A theme satisfying none of them fails the mandate.

mandates.statement: An absent fact renders visibly distinct from a false one and from a zero.
mandates.note: The kit's --unknown does NOT satisfy this: it is a freshness bucket ('no date'), not 'no reading was taken'. It is recorded under the freshness-ramp role, where it belongs.

roles.what: Primary text ink.
Second text luminance — supporting content, still body-grade.
roles.note: NERV and AKIRA independently chose --ink-2 over the kit's --ink-soft. Two-thirds of the graded set spell it the losing way; the kit-incumbent rule still wins because renaming one kit file is cheaper than renaming two theme pages plus every consumer of --ink-soft.

roles.what: AA-measured small-text metadata ink. Contrast is a measured property of this token, not a guess.
roles.citation: AKIRA: '--ink-meta: AA small-text ink on --stock (6.60:1, measured)'; WIRE: '--ink-meta: AA metadata token, measured on all 4 grounds'; NERV: '--nv-meta: AA small-text token — primary chrome text. measured, §06'

roles.what: Ink that is NEVER allowed to carry text — hairlines, ticks, grids, dots.
roles.citation: NERV: '--nv-faint: NON-TEXT, EVER: hairlines, ticks, grid, redaction ground'; WIRE: '--ink-faint: NON-TEXT ONLY — rules, rings, ticks'
roles.note: AKIRA has no separate non-text ink; it draws rules in --ink-2, the same token it uses for secondary TEXT. That is the exact confusion the role exists to prevent, so AKIRA's absence is a gap, not a style choice.

roles.what: The ground of the page itself, outside any plate or card.
roles.citation: NERV: '--nv-void: the canvas outside any plate'; WIRE: 'GROUNDS — depth by light level'; AKIRA: '--stock: newsprint white — the only page ground'
roles.note: NAME COLLISION, and the sharpest argument for this contract existing: --void means PAGE GROUND in NERV and WIRE, while AKIRA's --void-edge means ABSENCE. One spelling, two unrelated roles, across three files written the same week.

roles.what: The ground of a content plate/card sitting on the page ground.
roles.note: AKIRA has no card ground on purpose — the riso aesthetic puts content directly on --stock and frames it with rule weight instead.

roles.what: The ground of CHROME — head/foot strips, rails, furniture. Distinct from a content plate so that 'this region holds no fact' is a token-level decision.
roles.citation: NERV: '--nv-band: strip ground — head + foot chrome bands'; AKIRA: '--mass: the black mass — chrome ground'; WIRE: '--panel-chrome: chrome plane — matte, never lit'

roles.what: The colour of a hairline/rule.
roles.note: AKIRA draws every rule in currentColor / --ink-2 and varies WEIGHT instead of colour — see rule-weight-scale.

roles.what: The base hairline width, as a token rather than a literal 1px.
A LADDER of border widths (>=3 steps), so weight can be a meaning-bearing channel.
roles.citation: AKIRA: 'ROLE: RULE WEIGHT [NEW — the contract has no border-width scale]'
roles.note: AKIRA ships 4 steps (--w-hair/--w-rule/--w-bar/--w-mass), WIRE 3 (--rule-w/-2/-spine). NERV has exactly one width and is counted as NOT having the scale.

roles.what: Monospace family.
Sans family.
roles.note: NERV is mono-only by design (terminal-bureaucratic). Its absence here is a deliberate aesthetic ruling, not an oversight — which is why this role sits at 2/3 and can never be a hard requirement without an exemption, and exemptions are forbidden here.

roles.what: A named type-size ladder, so a size is a role rather than a literal.
roles.citation: AKIRA: 'ROLE: TYPE SCALE [NEW — the contract ships only --maxw / --readw]'
roles.note: NERV ships 4 (--chrome-size/--body-size/--lede-size + a hard chrome ceiling), AKIRA 6 (--t-mega..--t-micro). WIRE ships none and sets sizes inline.

roles.what: Maximum page width.
Prose measure (reading column width).
Width of the gutter rail / furniture column.
roles.note: AKIRA has a .rail but sizes it from the grid with no token.

roles.what: Base step of the spacing ladder.
roles.citation: AKIRA: 'ROLE: SPACE [NEW — the contract has no spacing scale]'
roles.note: The kit's --sp-* landed MID-SESSION, after NERV and AKIRA were written — at authoring time the contract genuinely had no spacing scale, so NERV's --u* and AKIRA's --s* are independent inventions, not divergence from an incumbent. WIRE, written after, adopted --sp-* verbatim. This is the one role with 3/3 role evidence AND an independent-adoption receipt.

roles.what: Corner radius as a declared decision. All three authors argue that a radius of zero must still be a token, so that flatness is a choice rather than a default.
roles.citation: NERV: 'RADIUS — zero, everywhere. A token, so it is a DECISION not a default'; AKIRA: 'ROLE: RADIUS [NEW]. AKIRA's value is zero everywhere — but it is a value'; WIRE lists --radius-* under 'ROLES THE ORIGINAL CONTRACT NEVER NAMED'

roles.what: The focus indicator. A keyboard affordance.
roles.citation: AKIRA: 'ROLE: FOCUS [NEW — the contract has no focus token at all]'; WIRE lists --focus/--focus-w/--focus-off under 'ROLES THE ORIGINAL CONTRACT NEVER NAMED'
roles.note: The strongest row in the contract: 3/3 role evidence AND 3/3 name evidence, and for a while the only required role the kit did not have. Nobody could have inherited this spelling — three agents independently reached for the same word, which is why this was the one required gap that needed no human ruling to close. The kit now declares --focus, so canonicalBy re-derives as kit-incumbent; the WORD is unchanged, and was never in question.

roles.what: Focus ring thickness.
roles.note: AKIRA folds width into a shorthand (--focus: 3px solid currentColor), so its focus ring cannot be re-themed independently of its width. Counted as not having the role, which is the honest reading.

roles.what: A named stacking ladder, so layer order is a declared contract rather than an emergent accident.
roles.note: NERV 3 steps (ground/plate/strip), WIRE 5 (atmos/vignette/content/chrome/pop). AKIRA has no z tokens.

roles.what: MISSING — no reading was taken. Must render distinct from a zero AND from a false. The role INV_DS_MISSING_NOT_EMPTY depends on.
roles.citation: AKIRA: 'ROLE: ABSENCE [NEW — there is no MISSING role in the contract. --unknown is a freshness bucket]'; NERV: '--nv-null: NO SIGNAL — deliberately desaturated. an absence is not a hue'; WIRE: '--absent: grey — verdict: MISSING (never null)'
roles.note: 3/3 role evidence, 0/3 name agreement, and the kit has nothing. Naming this one is a design ruling (AKIRA's answer is a dashed EDGE, not a colour at all), so canonical stays null pending a human call.

roles.what: Checked-here vs trusted-upstream, encoded at token level.
roles.citation: AKIRA: 'ROLE: PROVENANCE [NEW — the contract mandates the distinction and gives it no token]'; NERV: '--nv-up: TRUSTED-UPSTREAM. CHECKED-HERE carries NO hue, by design'; WIRE: '--sig-mag: magenta — provenance: trusted-upstream'
roles.note: The context pack tiers --prov-* as AKIRA-only. By NAME that is right (1/3). By ROLE it is 3/3 — NERV encodes it as a hue, AKIRA as a border-style pair, WIRE as a second isoluminant hue. This row is the clearest demonstration of why the contract carries two separate evidence counts.

roles.what: Ruling frequency of a hatch/screen — a non-colour channel expressed as a token.
roles.citation: NERV: 'TEXTURE — the mandatory non-colour channel, AS TOKENS / the role the WARM PRINT contract has no name for'; AKIRA: 'ROLE: TEXTURE PITCH [NEW — the contract mandates a non-colour channel]'
roles.note: SEMANTICS DIVERGE and the contract records it rather than smoothing it: NERV VARIES pitch to encode (half/dense/void); AKIRA FIXES one page-wide ruling ('never varied for effect') and encodes with coverage instead; WIRE's --scan-pitch is atmosphere only ('Decoration; encodes nothing') — its encoding hatch pitches are hardcoded literals at 4px/5px/6px, i.e. WIRE meets the non-colour mandate through mark shape, not through this role. Three tokens with the same role NAME and three different jobs.

roles.what: Ink coverage percentage declared as data, so tone steps are countable rather than eyeballed.
roles.citation: AKIRA: '--cover-full: 100; declared as data, drawn by the .tone-* recipes'
roles.note: AKIRA-only. One agent's proposal, not convergence — but it is a BUILT proposal, and it is one of the three mechanisms satisfying INV_DS_NON_COLOUR_CHANNEL.

roles.what: Mark SHAPE carried as a token (mask image), so shape can encode meaning independently of the hue painted through it.
roles.citation: WIRE: 'ENCODED MARKS — mask carries SHAPE, token carries COLOUR'
roles.note: WIRE-only, 10 marks. NERV reaches the same idea in CSS ('mask-image for SHAPE + background-color for COLOUR — a custom property cannot be...') but does NOT tokenize the shapes, so it is counted as not having the role.

roles.what: One token per verdict state (holds / partial / broke), so a verdict is a role lookup rather than a colour literal.
roles.note: AKIRA deliberately refuses a verdict colour set — 'verdict plate — 4 STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT OBJECTS, not 4 colours' — and encodes verdict entirely through structure. Recorded as absent because there is no token, but the absence is a ruling, not a gap. The kit's --defect/--fixed pair is a different axis (defect vs fixed, not holds/partial/broke) and is NOT mapped here.

roles.what: Transition duration as a token, so motion is a declared decision and there is a seam a prefers-reduced-motion rule can turn.
roles.citation: NERV: 'MOTION — declared at zero. This artifact does not animate.' (--nv-dur: 0ms)
roles.note: CORRECTS THE PRIOR CENSUS. A substring probe for 'motion' returned 0 across all four files and the role was written off as 'declared missing by AKIRA, built by nobody'. NERV built one and spelled it --dur. The probe measured a spelling and reported it as a role — which is precisely the failure mode this contract exists to end.

roles.what: The single rotation angle a theme is allowed to use.
roles.citation: AKIRA: 'ROLE: GEOMETRY / TILT [NEW]. Exactly ONE angle exists.'

roles.what: Overlay wash behind popovers/modals.
::selection ground and ink.
roles.citation: WIRE lists --select-bg/--select-ink under 'ROLES THE ORIGINAL CONTRACT NEVER NAMED'

roles.what: Named opacity grades, so 'quieter' is a role rather than a magic decimal.
Vignette pooling parameters for the page atmosphere.
roles.note: NERV and AKIRA both HAVE an atmosphere (scanline field / paper tooth) but neither tokenizes it — the values are literals in the body::before rules. Counted as absent, because the role is 'a token exists', not 'the page does the thing'.

roles.what: Age buckets for a dated reading (fresh / recent / moderate / stale / undated).
roles.note: The kit's --unknown lives in THIS role ('no date'), not in `absence` ('no reading was taken'). Conflating them is the specific error this contract is built to stop.

roles.what: The single non-encoding accent hue (links, emphasis).
roles.note: NERV has no accent at all (its only hue, --nv-up, is a legended provenance signal). AKIRA's --red is explicitly 'ROLE: SIGNAL — the ONE hue. Never decorative' and is NOT mapped to accent.
